_comment: DRAFT -- NOT live, not in manifest.json, not loaded by either app. These are the three foundation levels of heresies's rebuilt curriculum; see CURRICULUM-PLAN.md for the full 19-level target shape (3 below + 8 existing re-sequenced + 7 bridging + 1 capstone). difficultyElo is computed for that final shape (totalLevels=19), so it needs no recomputation at cutover. Every citation is drawn from references already shipped and reviewed in the live bank; verified with onramp_tool.py check.

questions.prompt: Arianism denied what about the Son of God?
choices: That he is truly God, not a creature
That he truly rose from the dead
That he was born of the Virgin Mary
That he founded a visible Church
questions.correctAnswer: That he is truly God, not a creature
questions.explanation: Arius was willing to call the Son the highest of all creatures. The Church answered with one word -- consubstantial -- because sharing God's own substance is exactly what no creature does.
questions.hint: Arius exalted the Son highly, just not quite far enough.

citations.quote: The Son of God is 'begotten, not made, of the same substance (homoousios) as the Father.'

questions.prompt: True or False: Docetism claimed that Christ only appeared to have a real human body.
questions.explanation: True -- the name comes from a Greek word meaning 'to seem.' The First Letter of John already answers it: the spirit that acknowledges Jesus Christ come in the flesh is the one that belongs to God.
questions.hint: The name itself comes from the Greek for 'to seem.'

citations.quote: This is how you can know the Spirit of God: every spirit that acknowledges Jesus Christ come in the flesh belongs to God, and every spirit that does not acknowledge Jesus does not belong to God.

questions.prompt: Which heresy refused Mary the title 'Mother of God'?
choices: Nestorianism
Arianism
Donatism
Pelagianism
questions.explanation: Nestorius preferred to call Mary 'Mother of Christ.' The Church saw that the real issue was Christ, not Mary: if the one she bore is a single person who is truly God, the title follows.
questions.hint: The Council of Ephesus in 431 settled this one.

citations.quote: Hence the Church confesses that Mary is truly 'Mother of God' (Theotokos).
the holy virgin is the mother of God, not as though the nature of the Word had the origin of its being from the holy virgin

questions.prompt: St. John writes that every spirit acknowledging 'Jesus Christ come in the ____' belongs to God.
questions.explanation: The test John gives is bodily. Any teaching that makes Christ's humanity a mere appearance fails it -- which is why this verse was used against Docetism from very early on.
questions.hint: The test John gives is about Christ's body.

citations.quote: This is how you can know the Spirit of God: every spirit that acknowledges Jesus Christ come in the flesh belongs to God, and every spirit that does not acknowledge Jesus does not belong to God.

questions.prompt: True or False: Apollinarianism claimed that in Christ the divine Word took the place of a human soul.
questions.explanation: True. Against it the Church confessed that the eternal Son also assumed a rational, human soul -- otherwise Christ's humanity would be missing precisely the part that thinks and chooses.
questions.hint: The error left Christ's humanity incomplete on the inside.

citations.quote: Apollinarius of Laodicaea asserted that in Christ the divine Word had replaced the soul or spirit. Against this error the Church confessed that the eternal Son also assumed a rational, human soul.

questions.prompt: Match each early heresy to what it denied.

pairs.right: That the Son is truly God
That Christ had a real body
That Mary is the Mother of God
That Christ had a human soul

questions.explanation: Read together, the pattern is clear: each heresy subtracts one thing from Christ -- his divinity, his body, the unity of his person, or his human soul.
questions.hint: Each one takes away a different piece of who Christ is.

citations.quote: The Son of God is 'begotten, not made, of the same substance (homoousios) as the Father.'
Apollinarius of Laodicaea asserted that in Christ the divine Word had replaced the soul or spirit. Against this error the Church confessed that the eternal Son also assumed a rational, human soul.

questions.prompt: Gnostic groups generally held that the material world is evil. What does the book of Genesis say about creation?
choices: God found everything he made very good
God found creation flawed from the start
God left the material world unfinished
God made the world through lesser beings
questions.correctAnswer: God found everything he made very good
questions.explanation: The goodness of matter is the first thing Scripture establishes, and it is why the Church could never accept a teaching that treated bodies, marriage, or the created world as evil in themselves.
questions.hint: It is the line that closes the sixth day of creation.

citations.quote: God looked at everything he had made, and found it very good.

questions.prompt: True or False: The Church has always vigorously opposed the idea of rejecting the Old Testament.
questions.explanation: True. Christians venerate the Old Testament as true Word of God. Attempts to discard it -- Marcion's in the second century being the most famous -- were rejected every time.
questions.hint: One second-century figure tried exactly this and was condemned.

citations.quote: Christians venerate the Old Testament as true Word of God. The Church has always vigorously opposed the idea of rejecting the Old Testament under the pretext that the New has rendered it void (Marcionism).

questions.prompt: Which council condemned Arianism and gave the Creed the word 'consubstantial'?
choices: The First Council of Nicaea
The Council of Ephesus
The Second Council of Lyons
The Council of Trent
questions.explanation: Nicaea met in 325 for exactly this dispute. The word it chose was not biblical, which made it controversial -- but it was precise enough that Arius could not accept it, which was the point.
questions.hint: It met in 325, and its Creed is still recited today.

citations.quote: God from God, Light from Light, true God from true God, begotten, not made, consubstantial with the Father.

questions.prompt: Genesis closes the account of creation this way: 'God looked at everything he had made, and found it very ____.'
questions.explanation: This one word rules out every teaching that treats matter itself as evil. Whatever has gone wrong in the world, it is not that God made the wrong kind of thing.
questions.hint: The verdict God gives on his own work.

citations.quote: God looked at everything he had made, and found it very good.

questions.prompt: Chalcedon's four negatives answered two opposite errors at once. Which pair?
choices: Blending Christ's natures, and dividing his person
Denying his divinity, and denying his Resurrection
Rejecting the Old Testament, and rejecting the New
Overvaluing grace, and overvaluing free will
questions.correctAnswer: Blending Christ's natures, and dividing his person
questions.explanation: 'Without confusion, without change' answers those who merged the natures into one. 'Without division, without separation' answers those who split Christ into two subjects. The formula holds off both at once.
questions.hint: Two of the negatives face one error, two face the opposite one.

citations.quote: To be acknowledged in two natures, without confusion, without change, without division, without separation... concurring in one Person and one Subsistence.
Christ is confessed as 'perfect in divinity and perfect in humanity'... in two natures, 'without confusion, change, division or separation.'

questions.prompt: True or False: Monothelitism held that Christ has only one will, not a human will alongside the divine.
questions.explanation: True. The Third Council of Constantinople answered it in 680-681: two natural wills, with the human will following and subject to the divine, neither resisting nor struggling against it.
questions.hint: The name itself means 'one will.'

citations.quote: two natural volitions or wills in him and two natural principles of action which undergo no division, no change, no partition, no confusion... his human will following, and not resisting or struggling, rather in fact subject to his divine and all powerful will.

questions.prompt: Against Apollinarius, the Church confessed that the eternal Son also assumed a rational, human ____.
questions.explanation: Apollinarius had the Word take the place of exactly this. The Church's answer preserves a Christ who thinks and chooses as a man -- not a divine mind operating a human body.
questions.hint: The part of human nature Apollinarius had the Word replace.

citations.quote: Apollinarius of Laodicaea asserted that in Christ the divine Word had replaced the soul or spirit. Against this error the Church confessed that the eternal Son also assumed a rational, human soul.

questions.prompt: The Second Council of Orange in 529 condemned which claim about the beginning of faith?
choices: That it belongs to us by nature rather than by grace
That it requires the consent of a bishop first
That it can be lost once it has been received
That it must be professed publicly to be real
questions.correctAnswer: That it belongs to us by nature rather than by grace
questions.explanation: This was the Semi-Pelagian question: granted that we cannot finish without grace, can we at least start on our own? Orange answered no -- even the beginning is a gift.
questions.hint: The dispute was over who takes the first step.

citations.quote: if anyone says that this belongs to us by nature and not by a gift of grace... it is proof that he is opposed to the teaching of the Apostles.

questions.prompt: True or False: Pope St. Pius X described Modernism as 'the synthesis of all heresies.'
questions.explanation: True, in Pascendi Dominici Gregis (1907). He used the phrase because he judged Modernism to gather up the errors of many earlier movements into one system rather than being a single new claim.
questions.hint: The phrase appears in a 1907 encyclical.

citations.reference: Pascendi Dominici Gregis, Pope St. Pius X (1907)
citations.quote: we should define it to be the synthesis of all heresies.

questions.prompt: Match each heresy to the council that condemned it.
questions.explanation: Councils were usually called because a dispute had already become unmanageable. Matching them this way shows the Church working through Christology one contested question at a time.
questions.hint: They fall in the same order as the councils themselves.

citations.quote: the holy virgin is the mother of God, not as though the nature of the Word had the origin of its being from the holy virgin

two natural volitions or wills in him and two natural principles of action which undergo no division, no change, no partition, no confusion... his human will following, and not resisting or struggling, rather in fact subject to his divine and all powerful will.

questions.prompt: How did the Council of Trent describe the Church's reception of the Old and New Testament books?
choices: With equal affection of piety and reverence
With the New ranked clearly above the Old
With the Old kept only for historical interest
With each book weighed by its human author
questions.correctAnswer: With equal affection of piety and reverence
questions.explanation: Trent's phrasing matters: equal reverence for both Testaments. It closes off any reading that treats the Old Testament as a lesser or superseded book.
questions.hint: The key word in the phrase is 'equal.'

citations.quote: [The Synod] receives and venerates with an equal affection of piety and reverence all the books both of the Old and New Testament... as also the said traditions.

questions.prompt: True or False: The Church teaches that in the Eucharist the whole Christ is truly present -- body, blood, soul, and divinity.
questions.explanation: True. The formula 'body and blood, together with the soul and divinity' is deliberately comprehensive, which is what rules out treating the Eucharist as a symbol or as containing only part of Christ.
questions.hint: The formula deliberately names four things at once.

citations.quote: the body and blood, together with the soul and divinity, of our Lord Jesus Christ and, therefore, the whole Christ is truly, really, and substantially contained.

questions.prompt: The Catechism distinguishes the divine persons this way: 'It is the Father who generates, the Son who is ____.'
questions.explanation: The persons are really distinct from one another, and the distinction is in their relations of origin -- not in three separate gods, and not in one God wearing three masks.
questions.hint: The same word the Creed uses of the Son.

citations.quote: The divine persons are really distinct from one another... It is the Father who generates, the Son who is begotten, and the Holy Spirit who proceeds.

questions.prompt: What does the Church affirm against teachings that treat Father, Son, and Spirit as three masks of one person?
choices: The divine persons are really distinct
The divine persons are three separate gods
The divine persons appeared only in history
The divine persons differ in power and rank
questions.correctAnswer: The divine persons are really distinct
questions.explanation: The Church holds two things at once, and both are load-bearing: God is genuinely one, and the three persons are genuinely distinct -- distinguished by their relations of origin.
questions.hint: The distinction has to be real, not merely apparent.

citations.quote: The divine persons are really distinct from one another... It is the Father who generates, the Son who is begotten, and the Holy Spirit who proceeds.

questions.prompt: Why did the Second Council of Orange insist that even the beginning of faith is a gift of grace?
choices: Because claiming it by nature contradicts the Apostle
Because faith always begins with a visible miracle
Because only the baptized can begin to believe
Because grace is given only after long preparation
questions.correctAnswer: Because claiming it by nature contradicts the Apostle
questions.explanation: Orange's reasoning is scriptural, not merely procedural: to say the first movement toward faith belongs to us by nature is, in the council's words, proof of being opposed to the teaching of the Apostle.
questions.hint: The council grounds its answer in St. Paul.

citations.quote: if anyone says that this belongs to us by nature and not by a gift of grace... it is proof that he is opposed to the teaching of the Apostles.

questions.prompt: True or False: In Apostolicae Curae (1896), Leo XIII declared Anglican ordinations to be null and void.
questions.explanation: True. The judgment turned on the rite's form and the intention it expressed, not on the personal sincerity of anyone ordained under it.
questions.hint: The 1896 judgment concerned a rite, not the people who used it.

citations.quote: we pronounce and declare that ordinations carried out according to the Anglican rite have been, and are, absolutely null and utterly void.

questions.prompt: Pius X defined Modernism as 'the synthesis of all ____.'
questions.explanation: The phrase is a claim about structure: Pius X argued Modernism was not one fresh error but a system that drew together the errors of many earlier movements at once.
questions.hint: The word describes what the encyclical says it gathers together.

citations.quote: we should define it to be the synthesis of all heresies.

questions.prompt: What does Dominus Iesus (2000) say about treating the Church as one way of salvation among others?
choices: That it would be contrary to the faith
That it is an acceptable modern view
That it is a matter for each bishop to decide
That it applies only outside the West
questions.correctAnswer: That it would be contrary to the faith
questions.explanation: The document distinguishes respecting what is true and holy in other religions -- which Vatican II affirmed -- from placing the Church alongside them as one option among several, which it rules out.
questions.hint: The document draws a line the Second Vatican Council's openness did not erase.

citations.quote: it would be contrary to the faith to consider the Church as one way of salvation alongside those constituted by the other religions

questions.prompt: True or False: Leo XIII withheld approval from a set of views collectively labeled 'Americanism.'
questions.explanation: True, in Testem Benevolentiae Nostrae (1899). He was careful to say he was addressing the views in their collective sense, not condemning the American Church or its people.
questions.hint: The 1899 letter is careful about what exactly it addresses.

citations.reference: Testem Benevolentiae Nostrae, Pope Leo XIII (1899)
citations.quote: we are not able to give approval to those views which, in their collective sense, are called by some 'Americanism.'

questions.prompt: Match each magisterial document to the question it addressed.
questions.explanation: Three of these fall within a fifteen-year stretch at the turn of the twentieth century, when the Church was responding to a cluster of modern questions at once; the fourth revisits related ground a century later.
questions.hint: Three cluster around 1900; one is far more recent.

citations.quote: we pronounce and declare that ordinations carried out according to the Anglican rite have been, and are, absolutely null and utterly void.
it would be contrary to the faith to consider the Church as one way of salvation alongside those constituted by the other religions

questions.prompt: What does the Catechism say about the antiquity of infant Baptism?
choices: It is an immemorial tradition with second-century testimony
It began only after the Council of Trent in the 1500s
It was introduced during the later Middle Ages in Europe
It has never been the ordinary practice of the Church
questions.correctAnswer: It is an immemorial tradition with second-century testimony
questions.explanation: The Catechism appeals to explicit testimony from the second century, which is why the Church has treated the practice as apostolic in origin rather than as a later development.
questions.hint: The Catechism appeals to evidence from the second century.

citations.quote: The practice of infant Baptism is an immemorial tradition of the Church. There is explicit testimony to this practice from the second century on.

questions.prompt: True or False: The Council of Trent ranked the New Testament above the Old in the reverence owed to it.
questions.explanation: False. Trent says the opposite -- the Church receives and venerates all the books of both Testaments with an equal affection of piety and reverence.
questions.hint: The council's own word for the reverence owed to both is 'equal.'

citations.quote: [The Synod] receives and venerates with an equal affection of piety and reverence all the books both of the Old and New Testament... as also the said traditions.

questions.prompt: The Catechism states that the Church confesses Mary as truly 'Mother of God,' using the Greek term ____.
questions.explanation: The word means 'God-bearer.' Nestorius preferred Christotokos, 'Christ-bearer'; Ephesus judged that the substitution implied Christ was two subjects rather than one.
questions.hint: The Greek word means 'God-bearer.'

citations.quote: Hence the Church confesses that Mary is truly 'Mother of God' (Theotokos).

questions.prompt: Why was refusing Mary the title 'Mother of God' ultimately a claim about Christ rather than about Mary?
choices: Because it implied Christ was two subjects, not one
Because it denied that Mary was ever a mother
Because it made Christ's divinity begin at birth
Because it placed Mary above the apostles
questions.correctAnswer: Because it implied Christ was two subjects, not one
questions.explanation: If the person Mary bore is a single person who is truly God, the title follows necessarily. Refusing it suggested that the divine Word and the man Jesus were two who could be spoken of separately.
questions.hint: Ask what the refusal implies about how many subjects Christ is.

citations.quote: the holy virgin is the mother of God, not as though the nature of the Word had the origin of its being from the holy virgin
Hence the Church confesses that Mary is truly 'Mother of God' (Theotokos).
